Windows (mostly) determines what to do with files based on their extensions - .jpgs open in a viewer, .txt in note/wordpad, and so on. Changing it to .bak makes it (mostly) not-runnable, and signifies to you that it's a backup file.

Unless you have extensions off, in which case you probably clicked on BritneyNaked.jpg.exe.

*nix uses "magic," which (mostly) tells what kind of thing a file is by certain patterns within the file itself. man 5 magic for more, but basically you can run a text file, or listen to a jpg, or do whatever you want with whatever you want. :)

Adding to /u/Ah_Pook's response, man is the Linux command to open the manual for the parameters that follow it.

Typing man 5 magic in a terminal loads the manual for the 'magic' file format.
Here is an online copy of that manual, https://linux.die.net/man/5/magic

The number signifies the type of manual that is being requested, in this case '5' which is of type "File Formats and Conventions" (According to man man: https://linux.die.net/man/1/man))
